label: dense: any of {0,g,i,r,p,2,f,o,z} seen earlier in sequence
explanation: Dense feature (active on ~51% of all steps, nearly every sequence) in every phase. Weak at t=0-1, then roughly flat. Its main structure is a memory of whether certain tokens appeared earlier in the sequence, chiefly 0, then g, i, r, p, 2, f, o, z. Rates are highest when out_tok, next_out, prev2_tok or first_tok is one of these (out_tok=0 gives 99.7% rate). seen(that set) captures 92% of activation mass and 84% of active steps, but precision is only ~0.60 because many sequences that contain these tokens still give zero activation. The largest activations (max ~7.8) come in sequences that start with 0 0 and peak on a later v in the original phase, then stay elevated over <DEL> and the copy steps that output 0. Low-quartile activations are small and spread out, often in sequences with none of these tokens. Not a crisp monosemantic feature; time-only baselines (t>=2) score nearly as well (F1 0.68).

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token, by phase (copy phase: g, i, 0, r; input phase: v, k, e, 3; delimiter step: <DEL>) and the token being output, by phase (copy phase: 0, g, r, i; delimiter step: 0, i, r, g; input phase: ); timing cues that raise it most: t=2, t=3, L=3 & t=5.
